newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Malaysia shares capped by currency concerns.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Malaysia shares capped by currency concerns.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed higher for the second day on Thursday, but analysts and fund managers said the upside was limited because of lingering doubts over the direction of the local currency.
The benchmark Kuala Lumpur stock exchange composite index gained 9.71 points, or 1.07 percent, to close at 918.54 after hitting an intraday high of 921.16. The index rose 1.29 percent on Wednesday.
A Reuter poll of 10 research houses showed the local index was unlikely to breach 1,020 points over the next one to two months. The nearest firm support was seen at 874 points and resistance at 968.
The ringgit's recent slide would continue to keep serious investors sidelined, analysts said.
"It all depends on whether the ringgit crashes," said a trader at the international division of a local brokerage.
The ringgit strengthened slightly against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, trading at 2.7620/70 by the 0900 GMT local market close, against 2.7810/30 at the close on Wednesday in Kuala Lumpur.
The share index has shed more than 12 percent since late July, and nearly 25 percent since the start of the year.
"There has to be a rebound after all those sharp falls," said a dealer at a bank-backed brokerage.
"The index has to get past 950 before sentiment improves," said Chong Woon Chou, investment manager at Aberdeen Asset Management in Singapore.
The Reuter poll found a support level for the index ranging between 850 and 885, while resistance ranged between 930 and 1,020 for the near term.

"It could easily recover to 1,000 in the absence of foreign selling, but it will take quite a while, around one month. That's when I expect the ringgit to stabilise," said Ramlan Ahmad, senior manager at fund managers Commerce MGI in Kuala Lumpur.

Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said this week that Malaysia would take firm measures to curb Malaysia's ballooning trade gap. They have yet to spell out the details.
Key blue-chip issues were among the most actively traded, including Telekom Malaysia Bhd and Sime Darby Bhd, which gained 20 cents and five cents.
Malayan Banking Bhd and power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd were also nibbled at by local and foreign institutions. The stocks gained 10 cents and 20 cents respectively.
Market volume stood at 237 million shares, valued at 1.357 billion ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 342 to 264.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot August contract gained 5.1 points to 918.5 with 1,026 lots traded. September futures gained 7.6 points to 922 with five lots changing hands.
